title: Deleting related data
summary: What happens to dependents when the principal goes: cascade, set null, and restrict.

steps.title: Delete an author, and then?
body: Delete an author who still has books, and the foreign keys in `Books` point at nothing. The database will not allow that, so something must give. EF Core picks a **delete behaviour** per relationship:
| Behaviour | What happens to the books | Default for |
| `ClientSetNull` / `SetNull` | kept, foreign key set to `NULL` | **optional** relationships (`int? ShelfId`) |
| `Restrict` / `NoAction` | the delete fails | none: you ask for it |
The defaults follow the meaning: a book cannot exist without its author (required), so it goes with them. A book can exist without a shelf (optional), so it just stops being on one.

code: seed.Authors.Add(new Author { Name = "Herbert", Books = [new() { Title = "Dune", Shelf = shelf }, new() { Title = "Children of Dune", Shelf = shelf }] });
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: `AuthorId` is required, so the delete cascades: one author and two books, 3 rows. The shelf is the principal of a different relationship; deleting books never deletes their shelf.

code: seed.Authors.Add(new Author { Name = "Herbert", Books = [new() { Title = "Dune", Shelf = shelf }, new() { Title = "Children of Dune", Shelf = shelf }] });
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: `ShelfId` is optional, so removing the shelf keeps both books and sets their `ShelfId` to `NULL`. EF Core did it with two `UPDATE`s before the `DELETE`, because the books were loaded.

steps.title: Choosing the behaviour
body: Now deleting an author who still has books fails with a `DbUpdateException` (a foreign key constraint), and your code must deal with the books first. That is often right for **valuable** data: you do not want one click on "delete customer" to wipe ten years of invoices.

> **Tip:** `ClientSetNull` (the optional default) only nulls the keys of dependents the context has **loaded**; `SetNull` also tells the database to do it, so it works for rows you never loaded. Cascade behaves the same way: `Cascade` is written into the table as `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

steps.prompt: An `Invoice` has a required `CustomerId`. Accounting must keep invoices for seven years even if a customer is removed. What should you do?
options: Set `OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict)` and archive customers instead of deleting them
Delete the invoices by hand before the customer
steps.explain: The default cascade would delete the invoices with the customer. Restrict makes accidental deletion impossible; the usual design is a soft delete (an `IsArchived` flag) for the customer.

items: Order lines when their order is deleted
A user's sessions when the user is deleted
Posts when their (optional) category is deleted
Invoices when a customer is deleted
Payments when an account is deleted
steps.explain: Cascade for parts that mean nothing alone, set null for optional links, restrict for records you must keep.

steps.prompt: Make deleting a `Customer` that still has orders fail.
steps.explain: Configure from the dependent: an order `HasOne` customer, a customer `WithMany` orders, then choose `Restrict`.

steps.title: Safe deletes
prompt: The tests give you `Customer` (`Id`, `Name`, `List<Order> Orders`) and `Order` (`Id`, `int Total`, `int CustomerId`, `Customer Customer`, `List<OrderLine> Lines`), and `OrderLine` (`Id`, `string Product`, `int OrderId`, `Order Order`).
Write `ShopDb` (`Data Source=shop.db`, sets `Customers`, `Orders`, `Lines`) with these rules:
- deleting an **order** deletes its lines (the default for a required key: nothing to write),
Then write `bool TryDeleteCustomer(ShopDb db, int id)` (at the top) that deletes the customer and returns `true`, or returns `false` (leaving the context clean) if the database refuses.
solution: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=shop.db");
template: dojoDb.Customers.Add(new Customer { Name = "Ana", Orders = [new() { Total = 10, Lines = [new() { Product = "pen" }, new() { Product = "ink" }] }] });
Dojo.Eq("Ana has an order: refused", false, TryDeleteCustomer(dojoDb, 1));
Dojo.Eq("Ben has none: deleted", true, TryDeleteCustomer(dojoDb, 2));
Dojo.Eq("deleting the order removed its lines", 0, dojoDb.Lines.Count());
Dojo.Eq("now Ana can go", true, TryDeleteCustomer(dojoDb, 1));
public Customer Customer { get; set; } = null!;
public Order Order { get; set; } = null!;
hints: On a refused save the customer is still marked Deleted in the context: `db.ChangeTracker.Clear()`.
